title: Afaro data removal broker opt-out manifest
description: Describes one broker's public opt-out flow as data. A manifest never contains executable code. Every manifest records the public page it was built from, the date it was read, and a committed capture of that page.

id.description: Stable slug for this broker. Used in run logs and in the manifest filename.

name.description: Broker brand name as it appears on the site. Brands only, never parent companies.

search_url_template.description: The broker's public search interface, with profile placeholders in double braces. This is the same URL a person gets by using the site's own search box.

method.description: How the opt-out is filed. manual means the broker requires an account, a payment, a notarized document, or a government ID, and Afaro does not automate it.

profile_fields_required.description: Profile field paths this manifest reads, for example full_name or current_address.city. The orchestrator stops if any is missing rather than inventing a value.

recheck_after_days.description: The broker's stated processing window, in days, as written on the captured page. removal-verify waits this long before rechecking.

notes.description: Anything the person needs to know that is visible on the captured page. Empty string when there is nothing to say.

source_url.description: The broker's public opt-out page this manifest was built from.

verified_on.description: The date source_url was read and captured, YYYY-MM-DD.

source_capture.description: Path to the committed screenshot of source_url, relative to the manifests directory. The validator fails if the file is absent.

page_url.description: A public page over https. Loopback over http is allowed only for the checked-in smoke manifest, and the validator refuses it anywhere else.

selector.description: How to find the control on the page. Prefer the visible label. A CSS selector is a fallback that is expected to drift.

label.description: The visible text on the captured page. Must appear in the capture.

verification.description: How to tell later whether the listing is gone.

url_template.description: Required when method is status_page. Profile placeholders in double braces.

success_when.description: Plain description of what a removed listing looks like, taken from the captured page or from the search result page.

id_requirements.description: What the broker demands beyond the form. Any kind listed here makes this broker method manual.

step_find_listing.description: Identify the person's own listing in the broker's public search results. Never a direct result-endpoint URL.

value_from.description: Profile field path. The orchestrator stops if the field is missing.

value_literal.description: A fixed value the form needs, for example a reason code offered by the page itself.

value_from_listing.description: Take the value from the listing an earlier find_listing step identified, not from the profile. url is that listing's address as the browser shows it. Brokers that key an opt-out to one listing ask for exactly this, and no profile can hold it. The validator refuses this without a find_listing step before it.

step_wait_for_email_confirm.description: The broker says it sends a confirmation email. The person opens it themselves.

step_read_email_confirm.description: Phase 1. Read the broker's confirmation email from the person's own connected mailbox and open the link. Defined here so Phase 1 adds behavior, not schema.

link_text.description: The visible text of the confirmation link, as described on the captured page.

step_human_gate.description: Hand the step to the person. reason submit is the guided-mode approval before anything is sent. The other four are steps no mode passes on its own.

prompt.description: What the person is being asked to do, in plain words.
